approach: Find the common speed at 1 s, then track each block's free motion after the string goes slack until their positions again satisfy the fixed string length.

steps.text: Released from rest, the system accelerates at a = (m2 − m1)g/(m1 + m2), so at t = 1 s both blocks have the same speed v = a × 1.
When the 2 kg block is suddenly stopped, its speed drops to zero while the 1 kg block still moves upward at speed v, so the string cannot stay taut and goes slack.
steps.equation: string slack: both blocks now move under gravity alone

steps.text: After the stop, the 1 kg block rises then falls freely from initial upward speed v, and the 2 kg block falls freely from rest.
steps.equation: x1(t') = −v t' + ½g t'², x2(t') = ½g t'²  (downward positive)

steps.text: The string becomes tight again when the sum of the two downward displacements returns to zero, restoring the original taut length.
Solve for the nonzero root, using v = g/3.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the string stays taut so the 1 kg block also stops instantly gives 0 s; this misses that a string cannot push, so the block keeps moving and the string goes slack.
Treating only the 1 kg block's motion and ignoring that the 2 kg block also falls freely during the slack period gives t' = 2v/g = 2/3 s.
